claim.claim-text: 1. A method of forming an insulation board assembly, comprising:

2. The method of claim 1, wherein a bottom surface of the first roll of facer material is in direct contact with the foam insulation board, and wherein a top surface of the second roll of facer material is in direct contact with the foam insulation board during the application.
3. The method of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material comprise yarns or tapes.
4. The method of claim 3, wherein the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material comprises yarns or tapes made from synthetic polymers.

5. The method of claim 3 or claim 4, wherein the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material each have a warp density from 4 to 30 ends per 25.4 mm (per inch) and a weft density from 4 to 30 picks per 25.4 mm (per inch).

6. The method of any one of claims 1 to 5, wherein the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material each have a tongue tear strength of over 67 N (15 lbt) in both a machine direction and a cross direction.

7. The method of any one of claims 1 to 6, wherein the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material each comprise woven polypropylene, propylene alpha-olefin copolymers or ethylene alpha-olefin copolymers.
8. The method of any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the first roll of facer material and second roll of facer material comprise no glass fibers.
9. The method of any one of claims 1 to 8, wherein the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material each have a thickness of 0.05 mm (2 mil) to 1.27 mm (50 mil).
10. The method of any one of claims 1 to 9, wherein the foam insulation board is a polyisocyanurate or polyurethane foam.
11. The method of any one of claims 1 to 10, wherein the foam insulation board has a density of 8 to 96 kg/m<3> (0.5 to 6.0 pcf).
12. The method of any one of claims 1 to 11, wherein the roof assembly consists of a roof membrane, a bonding adhesive and the foam insulation board.
13. The method of claim 1, further comprising: applying a polymer coating on one or both side of one or both of the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material.
14. The method of claim 1, further comprising: laminating a non-woven material on one or both side of one or both of the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer material.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein the non-woven material is laminated to the first roll of facer material and/or the second roll of facer material via adhesive or a tie layer.

16. The method of claim 14 or claim 15, wherein the non-woven material is selected from the group consisting of polyester, polyethylene, ethylene alpha-olefin copolymers, polypropylene, propylene alpha-olefin copolymers, nylon, glass, Kevlar, basalt, and carbon fiber.

17. The method of claim 1, further comprising: laminating one or both sides of one or both of the first roll of facer material and the second roll of facer with a glass mat, a glass scrim or a coated glass scrim.

18. The method of any one of claims 1 to 17, further comprising: adhering or mechanically fastening the insulation board assembly onto the roof assembly such that the roof assembly meets the Very Severe Hail rating of FM 4470 (Class 1).
